title: 3 productivity myths that are costing you hours
hook: Three productivity myths that cost you hours.

points.label: MYTH
points.say: Myth one. Multitasking gets more done.

points.label: REALITY
points.note: Every switch costs you up to 20 minutes of focus.
points.say: Reality. Every context switch costs up to twenty minutes of focus. You are not doing two things at once, you are doing both badly.

points.label: MYTH
points.note: A longer to-do list means a more productive day.
points.say: Myth two. A longer to-do list means a more productive day.

points.label: REALITY
points.note: Three real priorities beat twenty vague ones.
points.say: Reality. Three real priorities beat twenty vague ones. A long list is procrastination that looks like planning.

outro: Cut the list. Protect the focus.
caption:
Three productivity myths that quietly cost you hours — and what the research actually says.

Multitasking isn't doing two things at once, it's doing both badly. And a twenty-item list is usually procrastination wearing a suit.

Which one were you guilty of this week?
